sources.entry: DCPerf: An Open-Source, Battle-Tested Performance Benchmark Suite for Datacenter Workloads - Shows standard suites misproject data-centre servers, and states the fleet-matching method the suite is built by.

summary.title: DCPerf: An Open-Source, Battle-Tested Performance Benchmark Suite for Datacenter Workloads
summary.one_liner: Learn why standard benchmarks like SPEC CPU and CloudSuite mis-project datacenter server performance, and how Meta's open-source DCPerf suite models production workloads to match fleet performance within a 3.3% error margin.
keywords: how to benchmark cpus for datacenters
takeaways: Standard suites such as SPEC CPU 2017 can overestimate production server performance; the paper reports a 28% overestimate for Meta's latest SKU.
DCPerf models workload categories (web, data caching, big data, media processing, ranking) with production-like software architecture, threading, and traffic patterns.
Fidelity is checked at the microarchitecture level too (IPC, cache misses, branch misprediction, memory bandwidth, power), not just throughput and latency.
The suite is designed to run on one or a few servers with three steps: clone, build, run.
The paper reports projections within a 3.3% error across four server generations (36 to 176 cores).
summary.summary: The paper introduces DCPerf, Meta's open-source benchmark suite used to inform CPU procurement for millions of servers. It argues that SPEC CPU and CloudSuite misrepresent datacenter workloads, especially on many-core machines, and describes requirements such as easy deployment outside Meta and high fidelity to production software architecture and traffic. It details the framework (automation, result reporting, hooks for metrics) and the benchmarks (MediaWiki, DjangoBench, FeedSim, TaoBench, SparkBench, VideoTranscode), and reports fidelity and real-world impact such as a 38% web app gain from vendor optimizations.
